_comment: Macro benchmark baseline: four bots replaying the standard session.
Regenerate: bot bench --rounds 360 --json benches/macro-baseline.json
Gate: CI fails if p99 exceeds 2x this value, or 5% of a tick, whichever
is larger (bot::bench::REGRESSION_FACTOR and NOISE_FLOOR_US).
The workload fields are checked, not decorative: comparing a run at a
different --rounds measures the parameters rather than the server.
HARDWARE MATTERS. These came from the machine named below; a CI runner is
different silicon and was measured at 1.65x this machine on the previous
workload. That is why the floor exists: twice a p99 this small is inside a
shared runner's scheduling noise.
REBASELINED 2026-08-19, and for the SECOND time because the WORKLOAD moved
rather than the server. That is now a pattern worth naming: this benchmark
is a fixed script measured against a game that keeps changing, so any
commit that alters how long an action takes silently alters what is being
measured. Check the tick count before believing a p99.
What happened this time. `04652ca` made a chiselled sub-node cost a
thirteen-and-a-half-th of its material instead of a whole block, which is
the behaviour it was written to change - and the standard session chisels
every fourth round. The session got FASTER and therefore SHORTER: 622
ticks to 379 at the old --rounds 120. p99 is the fourth-worst tick of 379
where it was the seventh-worst of 622, so it moved from 358 us to ~3500
while the worst tick itself did not move at all (7900 us against 7869) and
the total tick time FELL. Nightly read that as a 15x regression for three
nights. Nothing had regressed.
So --rounds went 120 to 360, restoring ~626 ticks, and p99 came back to
the hundreds of microseconds on its own - which is the measurement that
proves the reading above rather than merely asserting it.
RECORDED FROM A MEDIAN OF FIVE RUNS, not one. Single runs are how the
investigation above went wrong twice: a bisect over one sample per commit
named an innocent commit (source renewal, `928665c`, cleared at 683/745/697
us against a parent at 674/584/415), and one 1615 us reading was reported
as a steady regression before repeats showed the distribution is bimodal.
mean, p50 and p95 are stable run to run; p99 is NOT, because it lands in
the join burst - four players arriving in one tick, generating and encoding
terrain none of them has seen. The five p99 readings here were 578, 707,
1027, 1366 and 1612 us. Take the median, and take it from a quiet machine.
_machine: dev container, AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, release build
